rounds.title: Round 1 · truth fixes
rounds.note: Same model (GPT-6 Luna, medium effort), same picture, and the same instructions except one sentence about drawings the solver cannot solve, which none of these ten is. Four of the ten sheets are word-for-word identical between the versions, so those pairs show how much the model varies on its own.

rounds.title: Round 2 · v4: link jobs, family check, schematic filmstrip
rounds.note: Same model and effort. v4 changes the fact sheet a lot and the prompt a little (see Results), so every sheet differs. Both sides are each version's first asking; v4 was asked twice, and the second asking differs in places (the Four-Bar's second asking names wipers, the Wiper's names no uses).

Hood_Hinge.why: v4 says it is a Stephenson six-bar that resembles a car hood hinge and names car hood hinges as the use, in both askings; v3 calls it a triple-rocker four-bar and suggests windshield wiper linkages.

Cylinder_Boom.why: v4's first asking puts no part name in bold, so the panel cannot point at any part (its second asking does); v3 reads as well and names excavator booms.

rounds.title: Round 3 · v5 on fresh mechanisms
rounds.note: Fresh mechanisms: eight library templates not used before, ten mechanisms students sent with feedback (five with a stated goal), and three test cases. Both sides are each version's first asking; v5 was also asked a second time.

Aircraft_Landing_Gear.why: v5 says it looks like an aircraft landing-gear retraction mechanism and names retractable landing gear, in both askings; v4f calls it a triple-rocker four-bar and names no use.

Excavator_Bucket.why: v5 recognizes an excavator bucket linkage in both askings; v4f calls it a cylinder-driven beam mechanism and names no use.

Radial_Engine.why: v5 says a five-cylinder radial engine in both askings; v4f calls it a five-slider slider-crank assembly and names no use.

Oscillating_Fan.why: v5 recognizes an oscillating fan and names pedestal and table fans (its second asking missed it); v4f names windshield wipers.

Elliptical_Trammel.why: v5 names a crossed-slot trammel; v4f says only "two-slider arrangement". (v5's second asking said Scotch yoke, which is wrong.)

Car_Steering.why: v5 says it looks like paired windshield-wiper linkages, in both askings, despite the wheels in the background image: a confident wrong recognition. v4f says nothing wrong.

Toggle_Clamp.why: v4f says it resembles a hand-operated toggle clamp and names toggle clamps; v5's first asking calls it a slow-return crank rocker for power hacksaws (its second asking did say toggle clamp).

student-196bdb37388f.why: Only v4f tells the student that PMKS+ refuses the input at A because three bodies meet there, which is what their message was asking about; v5 describes the motion and leaves that out.

student-19bc32785b6b.why: Nearly the same note; both read the Scott Russell attempt as a plain slider-crank.

student-19afdedcc1a4.why: Both describe the structure of the stuck drawing and neither sees a Strider attempt.

student-19716c16710b.why: Both describe the two unconnected bars the same way; neither sees a door opener.

student-1943d7a31665.why: Both list the links of the stuck drawing and say its motion is unknown.
